title: SAML IdP-Initiated Web Browser SSO
subtitle: The user starts on the IdP portal, clicks an app tile, and the IdP posts an unsolicited assertion to the SP — no AuthnRequest, and no InResponseTo to correlate.

steps.label: Click an app tile on the IdP portal
steps.lede: The user is already on the IdP portal and launches an application. The SP is never visited first — this is the defining shape of IdP-initiated SSO.
steps.devtools: Open DevTools (F12) → Network, enable Preserve log, keep Disable cache on. The tell-tale of this flow is what you will not see: no SAMLRequest anywhere.

steps.label: Launch the tile (no AuthnRequest)
steps.lede: Clicking the tile issues a plain GET to the IdP's launch endpoint. The IdP will build the response entirely on its own — there is no request message on the wire.
steps.devtools: Find the GET to /app/launch/…. Confirm there is no SAMLRequest query param — that absence is the whole point. The IdP is the origin of the flow.

steps.label: Submit credentials (often skipped)
steps.lede: If the portal session is already live this step does not happen at all. Otherwise the user authenticates against the IdP before the tile can launch.
steps.devtools: Under a live portal session there is no credential POST — you jump straight to the ACS. Otherwise you will see username/password/otp posted to the IdP domain first.

steps.label: Auto-POST the unsolicited SAMLResponse
steps.lede: The IdP mints an unsolicited Response — no InResponseTo — and returns an HTML page that auto-submits it to the SP's ACS. RelayState is chosen by the IdP as the post-login deep link.

resp.json:
<html><body onload='document.forms[0].submit()'>
  <form method='POST' action='https://sp.example.com/saml/acs'>
    <input type='hidden' name='SAMLResponse'
      value='U1lOVEhFVElDX1NBTUxSZXNwb25zZV9iYXNlNjRfcGxhY2Vob2xkZXJfQkJC…'/>
    <input type='hidden' name='RelayState'
      value='cmVsYXlzdGF0ZS1zeW50aGV0aWMtL2FwcC9kYXNoYm9hcmQ'/>
  </form>
</body></html>

steps.devtools: The response body is the auto-submit form. RelayState here is configured per app tile, not round-tripped from an SP request — treat it as attacker-influencable and allow-list it at the SP.

steps.label: ACS receives the unsolicited assertion
steps.lede: The browser POSTs the SAMLResponse to the ACS. With no request to correlate, replay defence rests entirely on the assertion-ID cache and the short NotOnOrAfter window.

jwt.title: Decoded SAML Assertion (XML)
payload: IdP entityID — validate against IdP metadata before trusting anything
The ACS URL this Response is bound to
Unsolicited response — there is no request to correlate to; SubjectConfirmationData carries no InResponseTo either
Gates acceptance; Responder / AuthnFailed mean reject
Validity bounds — allow small clock skew
Ties to the SSO session — needed later for Single Logout

steps.devtools: Select the POST to /saml/acs → Payload / Form Data, base64-decode SAMLResponse (POST binding, no inflate). Confirm the Response has NO InResponseTo attribute and no SubjectConfirmationData/@InResponseTo — an unsolicited response must not carry one. Use SAML Tracer / Auth Inspector to pretty-print.

steps.label: SP session created, land on the deep link
steps.lede: If the SP's policy allows unsolicited responses and the assertion ID is fresh, the SP marks it consumed, creates a session, and redirects to the IdP-supplied deep link.
steps.devtools: The ACS answers 302 to the deep link and sets sp_session. If the SP is SP-initiated-only, instead of an error many SPs bounce the user into SP-initiated SSO with a fresh AuthnRequest.

steps.label: Signed in at the deep-link destination
steps.lede: The browser follows the redirect with the new cookie and the requested page renders. The assertion ID is now in the SP replay cache until its validity window closes.
steps.devtools: Nothing further on the wire. Re-presenting the same assertion is rejected as a duplicate assertion ID within the validity window — that is the only replay defence available without request correlation.
